directions.description: For every algebraically closed field F of characteristic 0, every integer k≥2, and every non‑zero polynomial n∈F[x], any set A⊂F[x] satisfying that ab+n is a k‑th power for all distinct a,b∈A must have size at most 6, except when n is a perfect k‑th power and A is contained in the principal ideal generated by a k‑th root of n.
directions.lean_theorem_stub: theorem conjecture_abs_bound {F : Type*} [AlgebraicallyClosedField F] [CharZero F] {k : ℕ} (hk : 2 ≤ k) (n : Polynomial F) (hn : n ≠ 0) {A : Set (Polynomial F)} (hA : ∀ (a b : Polynomial F), a ∈ A → b ∈ A → a ≠ b → ∃ c : Polynomial F, c ^ k = a * b + n) : Fintype.card A ≤ 6 ∨ (∃ (s : Polynomial F), n = s ^ k ∧ A ⊆ (s : Polynomial F) • (Set.univ : Set (Polynomial F)))
directions.proof_strategy: Generalize the determinant criterion and Mason–Stothers theorem to bound the cardinality of D_k(n) tuples, and apply the Combinatorial Nullstellensatz to rule out larger configurations.
directions.title: Conjecture on Absolute Boundedness of Polynomial Diophantine Tuples

directions.description: For all n, k ∈ ℕ, the number of intervals [x,y] in the greedy 1‑Tamari poset on Dyck_n such that the lower endpoint x has exactly k valleys equals the number of bipartite planar maps with n+1 edges and exactly k black vertices.
directions.lean_theorem_stub:
theorem greedy_tamari_intervals_valley_eq_bipartite_maps_black_vertices (n k : ℕ) :
    (Finset.card {p : IntervalGreedyTamari n | valley_count p.lower = k}) =
    (Finset.card {m : BipartitePlanarMap (n+1) | black_vertex_count m = k}) := by
  sorry
directions.proof_strategy: Use the recursive decomposition of greedy Tamari intervals into sum and product operations given in the paper and show that it matches the decomposition of bipartite planar maps by inserting a black vertex. This yields a size‑ and valley‑preserving bijection, which can be formalized by induction on n.
directions.title: Refined enumeration of greedy Tamari intervals by valley count equals refined enumeration of bipartite planar maps by black vertex count
